These images customize the launch screen of the Flutter scanner example on iOS. They belong to the sample application, not to the decoding engine or a separately installable scanner package. Change the launch artwork independently of scanning behavior, and follow the parent Flutter README for native build prerequisites and scanner usage.

The [QR code scanner](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/qr-code-scanner) and [barcode scanner](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/barcode-scanner) are QR Code AI’s browser scanning entry points. For the corresponding development route, the [QR code scanner Flutter guide](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/qr-code-scanner/sdk/flutter) and [barcode scanner Flutter guide](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/barcode-scanner/sdk/flutter) connect this documentation to the two product journeys. If a product page is unavailable, the instructions and references in this README remain the starting point for this source directory.

To prepare a fixture for the sample application after launch, use the [QR code generator](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/qr-code-generator) or the [barcode generator](https://qrcode-ai.com/en-US/barcode-generator). Keep the original payload with the exported image so that you can compare the scan result with the value you intended to encode.

You can customize the launch screen with your own desired assets by replacing the image files in this directory.

You can also do it by opening your Flutter project's Xcode project with `open ios/Runner.xcworkspace`, selecting `Runner/Assets.xcassets` in the Project Navigator and dropping in the desired images.
